div.head: VIII Atr 23
div.ab: And gif man gehadodne mid fæhðe belecge ⁊ secge, þæt he wære dǽdbana oððe rædbana, ladige mid his magan, þe fæhðe moton mid beran oððe forebetan.
And gif man gehadodne mid fæhðe belecge ⁊ secge þæt he wære dǽdbana oððe rædbana, ladige mid his magan þe fæhðe moton mid beran oððe forebetan.
And gif man gehadodne mid fæhðe belecge and secge, þæt he wære dædbana oððe rædbana, ladige mid his magan, þe fæhðe moton mid beran oððe fore betan.

Und wenn ein Kleriker mit Fehde belegt und angeklagt wird, dass er thätlich Todtschläger oder durch Rath Mordstifter gewesen sei, so schwöre er sich rein mit seinen Verwandten, die Fehde mit zu tragen oder an deren Statt Busse zu zahlen haben.

And if a cleric is charged with a feud and accused of having been a slayer by deed or by counsel, let him clear himself with his kinsmen, who must share the feud with him or pay compensation in his place.

And if a man in holy orders is charged with vendetta, and accused of having committed or instigated homicide, he shall clear himself with the help of his kin, who must share the vendetta with him or pay compensation for it.

And if a man in orders is charged with a blood-feud and accused of being either the actual slayer or the instigator, he is to clear himself with his kinsmen who must bear the feud with him or pay compensation for it.

And if charge of feud is brought against a member of the clergy, and he is accused of either murder or complicity in a murder, he shall exonerate himself with the help of his family, who must either share in the feud or make compensation for it.

note.seg: Erste Z. der Übs. berichtige: ‘wegen Totschlags beschuldigt’. ‘Rat’ meint hier Anstiftung; s. d. Gl 2 (u. 27); Sippe 16h. 19B. 20
Correct the first line of the translation to: ‘accused of homicide’. ‘Counsel’ here means instigation; see that word in Gl 2 (below 27); Sippe 16h. 19B. 20
nicht ‘soweit sie’ (Cosack Eidhelfer 20), sondern ‘da sie ja’
not ‘in so far as they’ (Cosack Eidhelfer 20), but ‘since indeed they’

nicht ‘für ihn büssen’ (Schmid), wozu, wie II Ew 6. II Em 1, das Personalpronomen kaum fehlen würde; ‘for it’ versteht auch Toller 305b. Unrichtig erklärt Phillpotts (Kindred 222), der Priester unterliege nicht der Rache oder Wergeldzahlung

not ‘pay compensation for him’ (Schmid), in which case, as in II Ew 6. II Em 1, the personal pronoun would hardly be missing; Toller 305b also understands ‘for it’. Phillpotts (Kindred 222) wrongly explains that the priest was not subject to vengeance or to payment of wergild
Cf. II Edw. 6; II As. 1, 3 f.; 6, 1; VI, 1, 4; 9; 12, 1 f.; II Edm. 1, 1 ff. for other references to the part played by the kin of a delinquent.
